'''Candenat''', officially the '''Republic of Candenat''', is a landlocked country in [[South Acrola]]. It is the [[List of countries and dependencies by area|eighth-largest country]] in Acrola and the [[List of countries and dependencies by area|55th largest country]] in the world, with an area of over     591,613 square kilometres (228,423 sq mi). The country is bordered to the north by [[Iquir]], [[Sattle]] and [[Viussi]], to the east by [[Othya]], to the south by [[Jathua]], and to the west by [[Taniduna]]. The population of Candenat is about [[List of countries and dependencies by population|27.33 million]], 47.19% of whom are estimated to be under the age of 16 in 1764. Its capital and largest city is [[Pavrette]]. The country has two official languages and four recognised regional languages, of which [[Gieselei]] is the most commonly spoken.

Candenat was part of three successive powerful and wealthy Southern Acrolan empires that controlled trans-[[Coroan]] trade: the [[Jia Empire]], the [[Rabiaren Empire]]. At its peak in the 1200s, the [[Rabiaren Empire]] was one of the wealthiest countries in the world. Besides being a hub of trade and mining, medieval Candenat was a centre of ___, culture and knowledge, with [[Salitau]] becoming a renowned place of education with its university, one of the oldest in the world and still active.

In the mid-17th century, during the [[Treaty of the Globe]], [[Emara]] seized control of Candenat, making it a part of [[Emaran Candenat]]; a brief federation with [[Jathua]] was formed, achieving independence in 1715. After Jathua’s withdrawal, the Republic of Candenat was established. After a long period of one-party rule, [[a coup in 1741]] led to a new constitution and the establishment of Candenat as a democratic, [[wikipedia:Multi-party_system|multi-party state]].

In January 1757, an armed conflict broke out in eastern Candenat, in which [[Tabri]] rebels took control of a territory in the east, and declared the secession of a new state, [[Tabrisi]]. The conflict was complicated by a [[Military coup in March 1761|military coup in March 1761]] and later fighting between [[Bespi]] and other rebel factions. In response to territorial gains, the Emaran military launched [[Operation Seae]] in January 1763. A month later, Candenati and [[Emara|Emaran]] forces recaptured most of the east, although the conflict continued. [[Elections were held on July 1763]] with a second-round run-off held in August, and legislative elections were held in November and December. In 1763 and 1764, two coups led by [[Pel Asima]] overthrew the Candenat government. A military junta has since ruled Candenat. In May 1764, the junta dissolved all political parties. In July 1764, the [[transitional parliament]] was granted a five-year presidential term, renewable without elections.
